## In one sentence

Mixed models represent both population-level effects and structured variation
among groups, while resampling uses the observed data to assess uncertainty.

## Mixed models

A random intercept can let each group have its own baseline:

$$
Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + b_j + \beta_1 X_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ij}
$$

where $b_j$ represents group-specific variation. Random effects are useful for
clusters such as sites, schools, subjects, or batches when groups are viewed as
arising from a broader population.

## Bootstrap and permutation

The bootstrap repeatedly resamples observations to approximate the sampling
distribution of an estimator. A permutation test rearranges labels under a null
of exchangeability. Both methods depend on the resampling scheme matching the
design; clustered data need cluster-aware resampling.

::: {.callout-important}
Resampling rows independently can be wrong when rows are repeated measures or
members of clusters. Preserve the dependence structure in each resample.
:::

## Check your understanding

Choose whether observations, subjects, or sites should be resampled in a study
with repeated measurements from several sites, and explain why.
